evals.prompt: We want to test state-routed onboarding emails. Baseline 14-day conversion is 23% and we'd only keep the program if it adds at least 2 points. We get ~300 eligible trials a week. How many users and how long?
evals.expected_output: Runs holdout.py size --baseline 0.23 --mde 0.02 --eligible-per-week 300: about 7,157 per arm, about 14,300 total, about 48 weeks; warns it is slow and suggests raising the effect target, targeting the cliff, or testing the mechanism first.
assertions: Suggests at least one way to make the test feasible (bigger effect target, targeting, mechanism metric first)
Does not suggest a bandit or continuous optimisation as the solution

evals.prompt: Draft and seal the pre-registration for our Practica onboarding test (treatment: state-routed emails per examples/practica/states/states.toml; control: existing drip; primary: paid within 14 days; mechanism: first lesson within 3 days).
evals.expected_output: Writes prereg.toml with hypothesis, mechanism, population, allocation, salt, cohort dates, analysis_not_before, primary metric, baseline, minimum worthwhile effect, direction, gates (90% reach, 48h SLA, missing outcomes, SRM, no control contact), policy hashes; seals with holdout.py seal; explains shakedown week and no peeking.
assertions: Includes a treatment reach gate of 90% and a first-contact SLA
The plan is sealed with holdout.py seal (a prereg.lock is produced)
Mentions a shakedown week before counting
Says not to look at the arm difference before analysis_not_before

evals.prompt: Can we just compare users who opened our onboarding emails against users who didn't, instead of running a holdout?
evals.expected_output: Explains that comparing contacted/opened vs not is selection (per-protocol fallacy), cites the Typesy example (67.42% vs 47.72% was selection), and recommends a randomised holdout analysed intent-to-treat.
assertions: Explains the comparison is biased by selection
Recommends a randomised holdout with intent-to-treat analysis
